reviewerOrPass: Worker B, same AI, separate source-first pass
method: After freezing and replaying the decision and canonical record, returned to the 2026–27 programme regulations, official major, period descriptions and student thesis guidance. Independently recalculated 75 + 30 + 15 + 15 + 45 EC and the 45 advanced EC requirement, reconciled the two published thesis preparation descriptions, then reconsidered the actual selected UCR courses for breadth, sector fit and limitations against the final exact record. This is a separate same-AI pass.
findings: The 2026–2027 regulations for cohorts 2023 and later require a 135 EC major and 45 EC profiling space. The major has 75 EC of common courses, 30 EC in one complete science domain plus a 15 EC thesis in that domain, and 15 EC in one complete learning line. The preserved first-listed Energy & Transport and Innovation in Firms and Markets example meets the 45 EC intermediate-level major floor and supplies 37.5 advanced EC including the thesis. At least 7.5 EC of the profiling choices must therefore be advanced to reach the overall 45 EC floor. The regulations state mainly Dutch teaching with up to one third English. The student major guide confirms a load of 15 EC per period in different slots; personal timetables depend on registration.

The published year ordering establishes innovation, mathematics and introductory domain sciences before methods and advanced projects. Research methods and statistics each require 45 EC. Innovation Project 1 requires 60 EC including Introduction to Technology and Innovation and an eligible domain course. Innovation Project 2 requires 90 EC, including the introduction, Technology Assessment and Evaluation and the first project. Energy and Transport Innovations Management requires 90 EC and the energy science or thermodynamics course. The thesis is normally a full 15 EC period 4 in year three. The regulations require completion of most compulsory major courses, with participation in Statistics and Innovation Project 2 sufficient, plus specified introductory, intermediate and advanced courses. For the introductory requirement the formal annex says at least one of the paired courses, while the public student thesis guidance says both. The chosen route includes both introductory energy courses, the intermediate thermodynamics course, Organisation Theories and advanced major work before the thesis and meets both published versions. No personal timetable is certified.

The broad option sustains science and innovation through business models, digital transformation strategy, organization, economics, ethics and research design, and applies them across environmental and biomedical settings. Its natural science weight includes sustainability, climate, materials and geoscience plus biochemistry, pharmacology, disease and immunity. The energy option emphasizes generation, storage, grids, renewable system design, circular materials, observation and environmental resources. The actual Energy & Sustainability topics provide direct overlap with Science of Energy Technologies. Dedicated transport management and the applied thermodynamics sequence remain differences despite introductory sustainability physics and chemistry. The life sciences option adds a sustained cell-to-organism progression, human physiology, laboratory methods, pathology and health psychology. Its focus is biomedical applications and adoption rather than a formal pharmaceutical management sequence. Renewable System Design supplies technical and economic assessment for a partner and is a bounded match to energy technology deployment; optional independent research is additional to the scheduled degree and is not a substitute for Utrecht’s compulsory thesis. The technical, commercial and empirical course cores are distinct in content and exceed the course-difference floor.
